text:
maya: customer ACCT-998 flagged a billing mismatch. dashboard shows ~12.3k tokens for Feb 4th streaming session but invoice charged 15.1k. they attached a client trace. escalating because they want explanation + short-term credit :grimacing:

alex: thanks — can you paste the session id and any client-side logs? does the customer use our SSE endpoint or web socket?

maya: SSE. session_id=ses_7f4a2c. client logs show cancel at ~18s (user pressed cancel). app then reconnected and resumed a new request. attaching server logs snippet below.

rachel: putting :eyes: on this. common root cause: partial generation + reconnect can cause duplicate token accounting if the server finishes a partial response while the client thinks it canceled. also we had a recently-deployed race fix that changed how finalization events are emitted (might be related).

maya: server logs (redacted):
```
[2026-06-12T14:03:15Z] session=ses_7f4a2c evt=stream.start model=gpt-l7 ack_id=az1
[2026-06-12T14:03:33Z] session=ses_7f4a2c evt=stream.chunk tokens_emitted=1845 bytes=12k
[2026-06-12T14:03:33Z] session=ses_7f4a2c evt=client.cancel reason=client_abort
[2026-06-12T14:03:33Z] session=ses_7f4a2c evt=stream.finish tokens_total=1850 status=partial
[2026-06-12T14:03:37Z] session=ses_c0d9aa evt=stream.start (reconnect, new request)
[2026-06-12T14:03:40Z] session=ses_c0d9aa evt=stream.chunk tokens_emitted=3200 bytes=20k
[2026-06-12T14:03:45Z] session=ses_c0d9aa evt=stream.finish tokens_total=3210 status=complete
```

alex: interesting — stream.finish for ses_7f4a2c with status=partial shows tokens_total=1850. That 1850 likely got counted by the metering pipeline even though client canceled immediately after chunk. Then customer reconnected and generated a new 3210 tokens. Sum -> ~5060 tokens for that UX. But their dashboard shows 12.3k vs invoice 15.1k, so discrepancy persists across multiple sessions; might be more duplicated partials or an aggregator bug during daily rollup.

rachel: quick repro I used (devbox):
1) curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams?model=gpt-l7 
2) wait 15s for a chunk to come, ctrl-c to simulate client cancel
3) immediately open a new curl and finish generation

observed: metering events emitted for both sessions. if we aggressively finalize partials in ingestion, we double-count some tokens when the reconstructor later merges KV prefixes. sending minimal repro script below.

alex: can you paste the SSE payload example they sent? esp the last chunk framing.

maya: SSE fragment from client (sanitized):
```
event: chunk
data: {"text":"...","tokens":512,"end":false}

event: chunk
data: {"text":"...","tokens":1333,"end":true}
```

maya: customer says they canceled right after the second "end":true chunk but before client ack. looks like server already counted the tokens and our metering had a window where a re-emitted prefix from the resumed session triggered additional accounting.

support_escalations: billing-bot ran auto-reconcile and produced a delta for account ACCT-998: dashboard_total=12287 invoice_total=15102 delta=2825 flagged_by=auto-reconcile-qty-check

alex: immediate actions I'd propose:
- run bin/export-metering --session ses_7f4a2c and ses_c0d9aa to get raw metering events (ingest+post-agg).
- check daily-rollup job between 2026-06-12T00:00 and 2026-06-13T00:00 for duplicates.
- if duplicates found, issue a temporary credit equal to the delta and notify finance.

rachel: long-term fix options:
- change metering ingest so partial stream.finish events are tagged as provisional and only committed after a 5s window that ensures no resumed session replays the same prefix.
- or dedupe at rollup using sequence hashes of (customer, conversation_prefix_hash).

maya: customer asked for ETA. can we do fast reconciliation + manual credit today?

alex: I can pull metering events now. will update within 2h. tagging @rachel for the provisional-flag design.

rachel: ack. I'll draft the rollout for provisional flag. small schema bump + 1-line consumer change. estimate 3-5 days for safe deploy.

billing-bot: action=credit_created account=ACCT-998 amount="$28.25" reason="metering reconciliation: streaming duplicate tokens" created_by=support_escalations

maya: forwarding this to the customer with the credit and a brief explainer. thanks team :tada:

alex: follow-up: created GH issue infra/metering#1429 with logs and repro. attaching label P1-billing.

rachel: nice. once we confirm root cause I'll add a regression test in the metering CI that simulates client-abort+reconnect flows.

maya: closing the thread for now. will reopen if customer pushes back.
